newsitem.title: USA: DLJ has stronger first quarter.
newsitem.headline: DLJ has stronger first quarter.

text.p: Investment banking firm Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Inc. Monday reported higher-than-expected first-quarter earnings, based in part on its mergers and acquisitions practice.
Earnings rose to $86.4 million, or $1.35 a share, well above analysts' consensus estimate of $1.06 a share.
A year earlier, DLJ earned $65.1 million, or $1.01 a share.
New York-based DLJ said total revenues in the first quarter climbed to $978 million from $775.9 million last year.

The company said its strong earnings were attributable to strong performance across the entire organisation and, in particular, the mergers and acquisitions practice. Growth of that unit contributed significantly to a 76 percent rise in fee income for the quarter, it said.
DLJ said its underwriting revenues in the first quarter rose to $173.9 million from $135.4 million a year ago. It said fee revenues rose to $146.1 million from $83.2 million.
DLJ also said that revenues from principal trading transactions rose to $156.3 million from $143.5 last year. But principal investment transaction revenue fell to $847,000 from $25.6 million.
DLJ's stock was unchanged at $37.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
